notes: Punctuation-only tokens like '-' or '...' : counted as words (whitespace split) or ignored (alnum-required / regex).
Contractions like "don't": one word (split / apostrophe-aware regex) or two (\w+ splits on the apostrophe).
Hyphenated compounds like 'well-known': one word (split / hyphen-aware regex) or two (\w+ and letters-only regex).
Tokens glued by punctuation with no space ('hello,world', '2,000', 'e.g.'): one whitespace token or several regex words.
Which characters separate words: any whitespace (tabs/newlines) vs. only the space character.
Whether purely numeric tokens ('1 2 3') count as words (letters-only regex says no).
Whether non-ASCII letters ('naïve', 'café') form single words (unicode \w) or get split (ASCII [A-Za-z]).
